Detailed Rationale

Crisil Ratings has reaffirmed its ‘Crisil AA-/Stable/Crisil A1+’ ratings on the bank facilities and commercial paper of Genus Power Infrastructures Limited (Genus).

 

The ratings are supported by a larger revenue base, stable operating margins and a working capital cycle that has started to shorten. Liquidity is adequate and debt protection metrics are comfortable.

 

Revenue has grown quickly as installations under long-term metering service contracts have gathered pace, and a growing share of billing now comes from customers outside the company’s own project platform. Operating margins have stayed within a narrow band even as the volume of field work has risen.

 

Crisil Ratings will watch how quickly receivables from state distribution utilities are collected, because delays there tie up funds in the business and slow the decline in borrowings.

 

Steady cash generation from operations, a further shortening of the working capital cycle and moderate reliance on external debt will be the key monitorables.

 

The ratings also reflect the company’s long record in metering, its ability to execute large rollouts and the revenue visibility from its order book. These strengths are tempered by the equity it must commit to projects under implementation and by its exposure to swings in component prices.

Analytical Approach

Crisil Ratings has assessed Genus on a standalone basis. The cash flow assessment includes the equity the company must contribute to the special-purpose vehicles (SPVs) that carry out its metering service contracts.

Key Rating Drivers - Strengths 

Long record and proven execution in metering:

Genus has been in the metering business for more than three decades. Besides meters, it offers installation, software and maintenance services, which gives it recurring revenue beyond one-time equipment sales.

 

The company runs several manufacturing plants and an accredited in-house testing laboratory, and it has supplied meters to a wide range of state utilities and private distribution companies over the years.

 

Access to funding through a strategic investor:

A large institutional investor holds a minority stake in the company and is also a partner in the platform that owns the project SPVs, which should make it easier to raise capital as new contracts are won.

 

Order book gives multi-year revenue visibility:

The order book consists mainly of long-term contracts with state distribution utilities to install, run and maintain smart meters, spread across several states. Genus supplies the meters and acts as the engineering and maintenance contractor for these projects, so the orders should turn into revenue steadily over the next several years. The contracts also require installations to be finished within a fixed period, which keeps execution speed in focus.

Key Rating Drivers - Weaknesses 

Equity commitments to projects under implementation:

Each service contract is carried out through an SPV, and Genus must fund its share of the equity as installations progress. These contributions will be spread over the medium term; a materially larger commitment than currently expected, or one funded largely with debt, would be a monitorable.

 

Exposure to component prices:

Meters depend on semiconductors and other electronic parts, a good share of which are imported. Price swings and currency movements can therefore squeeze margins, particularly on contracts where the selling price is fixed in advance.

Liquidity Strong

Liquidity is expected to remain strong. Cash accruals should comfortably cover scheduled debt repayments over the next year, and the company has unencumbered cash and liquid investments as well as access to sanctioned working capital lines.

Outlook Stable

Crisil Ratings believes Genus will keep its market position and a sound financial risk profile over the medium term.

Rating sensitivity factors

Upward factors:

  • Revenue rising well above current levels while operating profitability holds steady
  • Receivable and inventory days falling meaningfully, shortening the working capital cycle

 

Downward factors:

  • Operating profitability weakening for a sustained period
  • The working capital cycle staying long or lengthening again
  • Significant additional funding extended to group entities or project companies

About the Company

Incorporated in 1992, Genus Power Infrastructures Limited makes electricity meters, smart meters and gas meters at plants in Rajasthan, Uttarakhand and Assam. Its shares are listed on both the BSE and the NSE.
